correctness.rationale: The source's equal-length proposition gives every non-primitive product an odd exponent d>=3 dividing the common length and primitive-root period 2l/d. Two hypothetical partners of one primitive p give two periods satisfying Fine-Wilf; distinct periods force a gcd-period contradicting primitivity of the roots, while equal periods force the same primitive root and hence the same partner. Symmetry converts the published ordered-pair count into the edge count.

value.rationale: The source's central problem is to describe and count primitive pairs with non-primitive product. The matching theorem adds global rigidity invisible in the aggregate count: equal-length exceptional products never branch at a primitive word. It converts the published ordered-pair formula into exact edge and affected-vertex counts and isolates all equal-length exceptions as disjoint partner pairs.
